name: Tirun

anatomy.part: stern tip of the hull, the low left point where the upturned planks meet the water
rear planks, on the upper arch just above the stern
crown of the keel, the highest point of the upturned arch
bow-side rim, where the arch turns down toward the bow
midships, on the lower underside of the hull
bow foot, where the lantern's tether is made fast
the lit lantern hanging beneath the keel, ringed

myth: Tirun came home keel-up in the spring gale, with no crew aboard and her lamp still lit underneath. Hesk, who keeps count at the pole, went down the tally and found eleven names missing and no reel that had let them go. Tavo the Gale laughed when the old women asked him, and said he had only lifted the boat, not drowned anyone. Aun, who cut the string, would not say what he had seen. Ennu the Kite-Wright came with bone and cloth and turned the hull over to look. Under the planks there was a lamp, trimmed by someone careful, and nobody in the islands can say whose hands. So the boat sits up in Vel with its light under the keel. When the wind is wrong, the old ones say, you can see that light moving beneath it, like someone still bailing, still counting, still looking for the way home.
verse:
Keel-up in the dark,
a lamp still burns beneath her
no hands to bail her.
